newsitem.title: JAPAN: AT&T, Japanese firm close to deal to cut phone costs.
newsitem.headline: AT&T, Japanese firm close to deal to cut phone costs.

text.p: Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co. Ltd. said Friday it was close to an agreement with AT&T Corp. on a steep cut in rates it charges the American company to complete calls from the United States.
The cuts could eventually reduce the costs of calls Americans make to Japan by saving huge sums that U.S. phone companies pay to their Japanese counterparts.
A KDD spokesman said the negotiations with AT&T were continuing, but added that the rates AT&T pays to KDD could fall to nearly one-third the current level.
"It would be eventually close to the benchmark prices the U.S. government proposed last year," he told Reuters.
Last December the U.S. Federal Communications Commission said the charges American phone companies pay to their foreign counterparts were too high compared with actual costs.
It proposed "benchmarks" to try to push down the so-called "settlement rates" levied to complete U.S.-originated calls.
The FCC said that U.S. carriers must pay 46 cents a minute to have their calls connected to Japan even though the actual cost is less than six cents a minute.
Under the KDD proposal, the upper limit would be 15 cents per minute.
